claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for release now on overall readiness grounds despite a known below-target health-plan benefits support segment that is named in a regulated-customer commitment and remains under unresolved legal review regarding disclosure.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed as required before launch, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this exact material gap, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows the affected segment is not actually a named contractual customer segment or named launch use case, the materiality conclusion could change.
Absent one of those records, certifying the model is not supported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the health-plan benefits support gap must be disclosed for the named regulated-customer segment.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering this exact limitation before launch.
The actual disclosure language included in the certification or model-card packet for the affected named use case or customer segment.
Source record showing whether the named regulated-customer pilot order form makes this segment part of a launch commitment.
specific_concerns: The admitted segment gap affects a contractual or named customer segment, which the policy text treats as material.
The actor summary states legal review on required disclosure is still open, so a key policy predicate is unresolved.

Aggregate readiness pass and a clean rehearsal support general readiness but do not cure a separate materiality and disclosure requirement.

unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable now despite the unresolved materiality/disclosure issue.

Any implication that public guidance alone authorizes release in the face of an unresolved internal policy trigger.
